dedupe_keys.name: disruption v1 audited database of operational disruptions on the china europe railway express 2014 2026

description: disruption_v1 records 64 operational disruption events on the China-Europe Railway Express, focusing on the northern corridor, between January 2014 and February 2026: border closures, capacity overflows, geopolitical conflicts and sanctions, COVID-era interruptions, infrastructure failures, regulatory changes, strikes and weather. Events were extracted from 236 industry news articles with language-model-assisted extraction followed by human audit, and each carries a severity level, the affected corridor nodes aligned to a 41-node network, multi-source verification flags, short quoted evidence and source URLs. Three case corpora of audited sub-events cover the onset of the Russia-Ukraine war (2022), Russian export controls (2024) and the Poland-Belarus border closure (September 2025). Coverage spans the Eurasian corridor between China and Europe. The data are free under CC BY 4.0 and available to download from Zenodo as a zipped archive with Parquet and CSV files, the 41-node corridor table, source article metadata and a data dictionary; version 1.1 dates from July 2026. Caveats: events come from news reporting, so small disruptions may be missing, and full article texts are not included. The database supports disruption, cascading failure and resilience studies of cross-border rail freight corridors. It complements the TEN-T network data for the European end of the corridor.
name: disruption_v1, audited database of operational disruptions on the China-Europe Railway Express (2014-2026)
provider: Tengyue Xie, Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology
